Subject: Request: mid-contract top-up + payment phasing

Hi Hannah,

Hope youre well. Were planning an unplanned capacity increase for our personalization pipeline and need to discuss adding a mid-contract top-up (~35% uplift) to our current Dedicated commitment. Primary asks: a) can we co-term the added capacity to our existing renewal (Nov 1), b) what payment-phasing options do you offer (monthly vs. 60/40 split), and c) wed like to understand options for escrow or holdback in the event of quality regressions during the first 90 days.

Samir is leading procurement on our side (ccd). I attached a quick estimate from our forecasting team (well follow with formal numbers). Would like to schedule a 30-min call this week to go over options and timelines.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract top-up + payment phasing

Hi Clara,

Thanks for the note and the forecast. We can absolutely support a mid-contract top-up and co-term it to your Nov 1 renewal. High-level options I recommend we review on the call:

- Uplift mechanics: staged top-up (start at 20% for 30 days, then step to full 35%) vs. immediate add. Staged reduces risk and gives us time to validate perf.
- Payment phasing: full invoice on top-up date, 60/40 split over two invoices, or monthly invoice smoothing across the remainder of the contract.
- Escrow / holdback: we can offer a 10% escrow on uplift payments for 90 days tied to a small prompt-set regression guardrail; if RL metrics hold, escrow releases to Redwood. Legal will want precise guardrails.

Ive looped in Ben (pricing lead) and Lauren (account ops) to outline pricing and billing flows. Ill schedule a 30-min slot for Thursday 11:00-11:30 PT unless that conflicts — proposed calendar invite coming.

Quick ask for the call: can you upload the forecast spreadsheet to the Drive link you use for procurement (or send an updated attachment)? helps us baseline the uplift math.

Best,

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@cohortly.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir.k@cohortly.com>, procurement@cohortly.com
Date: 2026-08-02T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract top-up + payment phasing

Thanks, Hannah and Clara. Following up from our prep sync: I put together three concrete pricing pathways (attached as cohortly-uplift-options-v2.xlsx) that map to different commercial preferences. Short summary below.

1) Immediate add, prorated to Nov 1 + 5% uplift discount for multi-year commit (saves ~7% on incremental unit price if you commit to extend 12 months at renewal). No escrow required.

2) Staged add (30-day trial at 20% of uplift, then remainder), 60/40 payment split on the incremental spend, 5% holdback (escrow) for 90 days tied to a small set of production prompts we mutually agree on. If metrics breach the regression threshold, well provide pro-rated credits.

3) Monthly smoothing: add immediate capacity but invoice incrementally monthly across the remainder of the contract; includes an SLA credit buffer and a refundable performance voucher (held until 90 days). Slightly higher unit rate (~3%) to cover billing operationality.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Co-terming: we can co-term with no penalty but true-up of usage vs. committed units will occur at Nov 1; any shortfall will be creditable into a 30-day extension window.
- Legal/Finance will need a short term-sheet for the escrow mechanics; Im attaching a draft term sheet covering the holdback release triggers (redwood-risk-carveout-term-sheet.pdf).

Next steps suggested:
- Clara/Samir to confirm preferred path (1/2/3) and procurement timeline.
- If path 2 selected, well draft a one-page amendment + DocuSign and create the escrow account instructions.
- If path 1 or 3, well prepare an invoice schedule and update the hubspot deal to reflect the uplift.

Happy to walk through the attachment on the call tomorrow.

Thanks,

--
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Hi all,

Thanks for the clear options — helpful. After an internal review wed prefer option 2 (staged add + 60/40 split + 5% holdback). A couple of clarifications before we sign:

- Prompt set / metrics: well propose 120 canonical prompts (server-side scoring) and an allowance for up to 10 production-related false positives that trigger a review rather than immediate credit.
- Escrow mechanics: we need the escrow custody details and whether an external third-party escrow (bank or custodian) is required.
- Procurement timeline: Samir expects PO approval by 8/12 and asks for the DocuSign link and a final one-page amendment this week so he can route to legal.

Please send the one-page amendment and DocuSign link. Well attach the PO once the signature is in place. Also ccd here is our procurement mailbox for the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the call tomorrow at 11 PT.
